conclusion: In this queueing model with assumed costs, on 8 cores the big server sustained 1198 and 8 small servers 1413 completions/s, a gap that follows the assumptions (the big server ranged from 1398 at 0% to 1027 at 6% assumed per-core contention, and with matched store costs it was 1617 vs 1579), while killing the single server failed 30.2% of requests with 3s of majority-failed windows and killing one of 8 small servers lost 25% of in-flight requests with failures above 1% ending 0.4s after the kill.
setup: queueing simulation, assumed costs, seed 1818; request = Erlang-2 CPU 5 ms + one shared store read; vertical baseline: 1 instance with 1/2/4/8 cores (cap 8 is configured), in-process store behind one mutex (hold 0.4 ms, worker keeps its core while waiting), +3% CPU per extra core; horizontal baseline: 1/2/4/8 single-core instances, round-robin LB (0.3 ms each way), async single-threaded store (0.15 ms service, 0.25 ms hop each way), +0.3 ms CPU; sensitivity: vertical 8-core contention 0%/1.5%/3%/6%; matched: both use the async store, no contention, no hops; ramp: Poisson, x1.2 then x1.02 steps of 4s, observe 1-4s, stable = no errors, cohort p95 <= 200 ms (unfinished counts as over), backlog growth <= max(size, 2% of arrivals); kill test 10s at 70% of the weaker 8-core sustained rate, kill at 4s, restart 3s, health check 250 ms x2, no retries; wall-clock deadline 50s
caveats: These are outputs of a queueing simulation with assumed costs, not measurements of HTTP servers running on a laptop.
The baseline configurations use different store implementations and costs, so their throughput gap does not isolate vertical versus horizontal scaling.
The matched configuration changes store access, contention and hops together; it does not isolate any single cause.
One seed and short observation windows provide no estimate of variability or confidence intervals.
Reported sustained rates are the best tested passing points under the stated stability rule, not proven long-term capacity limits.
The failure comparison depends on the configured restart delay, health checks, spare capacity and absence of retries.
The horizontal in-flight cohort contains only four requests, so its 25% loss is not a reliable estimate of the expected fraction.
Instance termination does not test laptop, load-balancer or shared-store failure.
